The defendants were served with the summons of the suit on 22.08.2014 and has filed joint written statement on 23.09.2014 challenging the suit of the plaintiff pleading inter-alia as follows:
a) That the present suit is not maintainable as it is gross abuse to the process of law.
b) That the present suit is not maintainable as the plaintiff himself has violated the terms and conditions of the work order to run and maintain the drug de-addiction centre.
c) The plaintiff has not come with clean hands and has concealed/suppressed material facts.
On Merits, it is submitted that the proposal for running 20 bedded de- addiction centre was awarded to the plaintiff on the basis of bid document.

It was admitted that the plaintiff was engaged to set up and run a newly created 20 bedded drug de-addiction centre initially for one year from November, 2010 to October, 2011 and thereafter extension was given till December, 2011.

It is further submitted that the plaintiff himself stopped the services of the drug de-addiction centre before the department can take over it due to which it resulted in great disservice to the inmates &
creating CS No 14758/16 Bhartiya Parivardhan Sanstha Vs Department of Social Welfare Page No 11/44 admission difficulties for the department in the welfare activities in the said home.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that as per the work order awarded to the plaintiff, the defendant undertook to provide free of cost building space, electricity, water facility to the partner NGO.
It is further submitted that since there was no legal obligation on the part of the plaintiff to admit more inmates than the sanctioned capacity, no work order was placed by the department.
It is further submitted that plaintiff had never sought permission in advance to keep more staff for additional inmates from the department in writing.

It is further submitted that the amount released was to be in conformity with the numbers of inmates and consumed rate to the actual amount incurred on medicine/consumables/service provided which was accepted by the plaintiff and now the plaintiff is not adhering to the same.
It is further submitted that the additional inmates was reported only from March 2012 onwards till December 2012.

It is further submitted that the department had to calculate the rate for payment for additional inmates on per day per inmate basis and payment was released to the plaintiff for the period March,2012 to December, 2012 on the basis of the rate fixed by the department @ Rs. 119/- per inmate per day.
It is thus submitted that the present suit be dismissed.
